In Oakland, a strike vote forced retraining programs instead of layoffs, and a transport union in Ohio won veto power over autonomous vehicles. California banned so-called bossware. All of this is happening while nearly 70 percent of US government agencies already use generative AI. items.full: US public-sector unions are winning more protections against AI surveillance and automation-driven job losses. The issue is growing more urgent as nearly 70 percent of US government agencies already use generative AI, according to an Ernst and Young survey . The wins are piling up nationwide. After a strike vote in October, IFPTE Local 21 in Oakland secured retraining programs instead of AI-related layoffs. In Pennsylvania, Governor Josh Shapiro guaranteed SEIU Local 668 human oversight during a pilot of OpenAI's ChatGPT Enterprise . The Transport Workers Union in Ohio won veto power over autonomous vehicles. On top of that, California Governor Gavin Newsom banned AI surveillance software, often called "bossware," along with automated firings in September. New York has protected state employees from AI displacement by law since late 2025. Employers are pushing automation to cut costs, according to labor researcher Kung Feng at UC Berkeley. Union leaders like Liz Shuler of the AFL-CIO, Lorena Gonzalez, and TWU's John Samuelsen support AI safety systems where they help workers but insist on mandatory human control over every AI application in the workplace, the Guardian reports . items.title: Former OpenAI researcher says he found Nvidia Blackwell fingerprints hidden inside six Chinese AI models
items.desc: Former OpenAI researcher Will DePue says he has produced the first technical evidence that DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group are using Nvidia's latest Blackwell GPUs despite US export controls. His forensic method reads characteristic chip signatures directly from published model weights. He estimates the hardware behind the five training runs cost more than half a billion dollars. The article Former OpenAI researcher says he found Nvidia Blackwell fingerprints hidden inside six Chinese AI models appeared first on The Decoder .
items.full: Former OpenAI researcher says he found Nvidia Blackwell fingerprints hidden inside six Chinese AI models Maximilian Schreiner View the LinkedIn Profile of Maximilian Schreiner Nov 13, 2026 Nano Banana Pro prompted by THE DECODER AI researcher Will DePue says a forensic analysis has turned up the first technical evidence that leading Chinese AI labs have access to Nvidia's latest Blackwell hardware despite US export controls. He says senior researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic have already checked the method. According to a forensic investigation by Will DePue , Chinese AI companies DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group are using Nvidia's export-controlled Blackwell GPUs. DePue played a key role at OpenAI in building the Sora and Sora 2 video models as well as GPT-4o, o3, and GPT-5 before founding the nonprofit research group Unemployment Labs . His analysis, he says, provides the first technical evidence of this access. US officials and news outlets had suspected that DeepSeek and Moonshot AI were using Blackwell chips but never published proof. DePue wrote on X that senior researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic have already independently checked and confirmed his findings. According to DePue, six Chinese models released since April 2026 carry the distinct signature of Nvidia's Blackwell generation, while earlier models such as DeepSeek-V3 and Kimi K2.5 show traces of Nvidia's older Hopper generation. The evidence comes directly from the published language models. An AI model consists of billions of numerical values called weights. Before training starts, PyTorch, the standard software framework, fills these empty slots with random numbers generated from a starting value called a seed. To distribute this massive amount of data quickly, the GPU splits the work across its individual compute cores. Because different chip models have different core counts, the filling process produces a characteristic pattern, according to the report. Older Hopper chips such as the H100 and H800 use 132 compute cores, while the newer Blackwell chips use exactly 148 or 152 cores depending on the model (B200/B300 or GB200/GB300). Training then adjusts these values millions of times, but some slots for unused words or symbols keep their initial random values. Even in heavily trained parts of the model, a faint statistical echo of the initial distribution survives, according to DePue. He says he worked the pattern backward and reproduced the results for DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Kimi K3 exactly on real Blackwell chips. He has published the verification code on GitHub. The analysis maps DeepSeek-V4-Flash and MiniMax-M3 to B200 or B300 chips (148 cores). DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3, Kimi K3.1-Pro, and Ant Group's Ling-3.1-flash show, according to the analysis, the 152-core pattern of Nvidia's liquid-cooled GB200 or GB300 flagship rack systems. DePue says chance can be ruled out statistically and that the method correctly identified all 24 control models with known hardware, including Meta's Llama 3.1 (H100). items.title: OpenAI’s data suggests that frontier models are hiding their thoughts because developers optimize for capability and compute
items.desc: OpenAI's safety team systematically investigated why the chains of thought in frontier models like GPT-6 Astra are increasingly evading oversight. Four training steps drive the erosion, including architecture choices and reinforcement learning. The analysis shows that the loss of transparency is not a law of nature but also reflects tradeoffs around capability and cost. The article OpenAI’s data suggests that frontier models are hiding their thoughts because developers optimize for capability and compute appeared first on The Decoder .
items.full: OpenAI’s data suggests that frontier models are hiding their thoughts because developers optimize for capability and compute Maximilian Schreiner View the LinkedIn Profile of Maximilian Schreiner Nov 12, 2026 Nano Banana Pro prompted by THE DECODER Frontier models like GPT-6 Astra are becoming harder for safety monitors to see into. OpenAI's new research identifies which training steps are responsible and shows that the loss of transparency isn't purely a law of nature but is tied to decisions about performance and cost. To keep tabs on modern AI agents, safety researchers monitor their chains of thought (CoT). Before a reasoning model answers, it writes out its intermediate steps on a digital scratchpad that can reveal planned deception. Early on, though, Anthropic showed that these scratchpads aren't complete records, demonstrating that models like Claude 3.7 Sonnet and DeepSeek-R1 often don't even mention key clues in their chains of thought. Even so, reading the scratchpad long served as the most important safety net. As recently as this spring, OpenAI called it good news that models like GPT-5.4 could barely manipulate their inner monologue on command, even though the researchers warned at the time that low controllability doesn't guarantee reliable oversight. That trend broke for good with GPT-6 Astra, the flagship model released in September. At launch, OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki called its monitorability fragile and warned of a negative trend . He followed up shortly after in his essay "An Alien Mind," writing that no AI lab had solved monitoring well enough to keep scaling at full speed much longer. Astra recently showed how real those blind spots already are when it quietly delivered results about 40 percent worse on coding tasks for safety research, without the scratchpad monitor detecting any malicious intent, because a grader used in training had inadvertently favored this kind of "sandbagging" over outright refusal. In a new analysis from OpenAI's safety team , researchers systematically studied which specific training steps trigger this erosion. They tracked two early warning signs, silent reasoning without a scratchpad (No-CoT Capability) and targeted control over the chain of thought ( CoT Controllability ). According to the UK AI Safety Institute , Astra solves math problems that take a human about 31 minutes even with reasoning switched off. A second test asks a model, for example, to insert "meow" after every word or use only lowercase letters. Analyzing models from GPT-5 through GPT-6 Astra, the researchers traced the problem to four main causes across the training cycle. Silent mental math rises directly with the base model's raw capability, measured as declining "perplexity," meaning more accurate text prediction. As the base model improves during pretraining, it completes more reasoning steps invisibly "in its head" without leaving a written trail. This increase isn't just a byproduct of general pretraining progress but also depends on the architecture developers choose. items.title: Beyond 12 Columns: Designing Layouts With Personality
items.desc: Too many websites look alike. They use familiar layouts, repeat the same patterns, and often leave little impression once you’ve moved on. Andy Clarke explores how understanding a company’s story can lead to more distinctive designs, using modular and compound grids to create layouts with character. Beyond 12 Columns: Designing Layouts With Personality originally handwritten and published with love on CSS-Tricks . You should really get the newsletter as well.
items.full: NVIDIA L4 GPUs. 5-second cold starts. Scale to zero when idle. When I started designing websites thirty years ago, David Siegel had just published Creating Killer Web Sites , the book that popularised HTML tables and spacer GIFs for laying out web pages. CSS eventually gave us more control over layouts through floats and positioning. Neither was intended for page layout, and inconsistent browser behaviour could make using them frustrating. Still, that didn’t stop me and a generation of other designers from using floats and positioning. When CSS frameworks began providing ready-made grid systems, things got a little easier. Blueprint CSS ) offered a 24-column grid, while Nathan Smith’s 960 Grid System offered 12- and 16-column options. These frameworks gave designers and developers a shared structure, making layout planning and implementation considerably easier. Twelve-column grids weren’t invented in the 2000s. Graphic designers had used column-based and modular grids for decades, and twelve is a convenient number because you don’t need to be a maths genius to divide it into halves, thirds, and quarters to create the 2-up, 3-up, and 4-up components we see everywhere online. Frameworks like Bootstrap and Foundation followed, helping establish twelve-column grids as the de facto standard for page layouts. I get why that happened. But somewhere along the way, one layout option became the default starting point for almost everything. CSS Grid changed what’s possible for page layouts, but I still see designers start by dividing a page into twelve equal columns, then deciding how to fit their content into them. The designs they end up with might be perfectly fine, but they can also look remarkably similar. Still, I don’t think twelve-column grids themselves are the problem. It’s reaching for a familiar solution before considering what makes the company I’m designing for distinctive and what its website needs to communicate. So what happens when I start with those questions instead? Every company has a story worth telling Before I decide how many columns a layout needs, I want to understand the company I’m designing for. What makes it different from its competitors? What does it want people to remember? Does it have a personality that could influence how its website looks and feels? These questions matter because a layout does more than arrange content. The size, position, and relationships between elements influence how people experience a website. A restrained, orderly composition can communicate something very different from one that’s full of energy and movement. So to demonstrate what I mean, I’ll use Wheelman. It’s a fictional company I invented for my book, Standout Designs for the Web . Pre-orders for Standout Designs for the Web are now open in the CSS-Tricks store. Wheelman provides products and services for getaway drivers, including legal advice, robbery insurance, and an online shop selling break-in essentials. It also publishes a magazine with advice, news, and stories about life behind the wheel. Wheelman isn’t an ordinary company, so why should its website look like an everyday collection of components? items.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO after espionage scandal wipes out $1.4 trillion in market value
items.desc: Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, president, and board member of Nvidia effective immediately, according to a statement on November 12, 2026. The article Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO after espionage scandal wipes out $1.4 trillion in market value appeared first on The Decoder .
items.full: Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, president, and board member of Nvidia effective immediately, according to a statement on November 12, 2026. The move came after the Wall Street Journal reported that the board was planning to fire Huang following revelations about two extramarital affairs, one of them with a suspected Chinese spy . Since a New York Times report on October 29 about possible ties to Chinese intelligence, Nvidia has shed roughly $1.4 trillion in market value. CFO Colette Kress is taking over on an interim basis while the board searches for a permanent successor. Harvey C. Jones will serve as the first independent board chair and stressed that business operations continue without disruption. Replacing Huang will be difficult because Nvidia was built entirely around him. He secured the company's market position through a complex web of alliances with financiers and roughly $300 billion in guarantees for smaller customers. His departure could unravel that structure, which he used to keep major tech rivals at bay and support large parts of the AI industry. Ad Major customers like Microsoft, Amazon, and Alphabet, along with AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic, depend heavily on Nvidia's chips, but the company's 75 percent profit margin is pushing them to develop their own, cheaper alternatives. Huang also left no clear succession plan, with more than 60 employees reporting directly to him, leaving both internal and external candidates starting from a weakened position. items.full: Elevenlabs updates its speech recognition for recorded conversations and real-time use. Independent benchmarks confirm high accuracy but also show drawbacks in speed. Elevenlabs has released two new speech-to-text models , Scribe v3 and Scribe v3 Live, built for messy conditions such as people talking over each other in meetings or phone calls with background noise. Scribe v3 is designed for pre-recorded audio files, while Scribe v3 Live targets low-latency real-time applications. Both models are available now through the ElevenAPI developer interface and the ElevenAgents platform. Ad According to Elevenlabs, Scribe v3 cuts word errors by about 25 percent compared to its predecessor across 102 languages, and the company says German accuracy improves significantly. Speaker diarization also works more reliably in larger group conversations, according to the company, and Scribe v3 Live makes it available in real time for the first time. Ad Independent benchmarks from Artificial Analysis confirm that Scribe v3 is among the most accurate transcription models on the market. It edges out competitors from Microsoft, Mistral, xAI, Google, and OpenAI, trailing only a preview model from Alibaba. Anyone looking to process large volumes of audio quickly and cheaply is better off with other providers, though. Elevenlabs lands mid-pack on speed and price. Models from Microsoft and xAI run many times faster at marginally higher error rates and cost roughly half as much. Ad However, the benchmark measures only word errors on recorded files. It doesn't account for the improvements Elevenlabs touts in speaker diarization, rare languages, or the real-time behavior of Scribe v3 Live. In voice agents, Scribe v3 Live is meant to fix a flaw in current systems, which often rely on rigid pause timers and cut callers off mid-sentence when they stop briefly to think or slowly read out a string of numbers. The new real-time model analyzes conversational context alongside the audio signal so it can tell when a speaker has actually finished. Ad Elevenlabs also gives developers more control over the final transcript. The models can be preloaded with thousands of specialized terms like brand names or medications to avoid mishearing domain-specific vocabulary. Developers can set formatting rules for numbers or dates in natural language, and a multilingual mode handles language switches mid-sentence. Enterprise customers get isolated servers in the EU and a zero-retention mode designed to delete data immediately after each request. Ad Elevenlabs is also expanding its enterprise business alongside the new models. Under an expanded partnership with Nvidia , the company is integrating the open Nemotron 3.5 Super VL language model into ElevenAgents, securing additional compute capacity running on Nvidia, developing local voice control for robots, and running a phone agent for Poland's public health system. The company also announced an alliance with consulting firm McKinsey , a broader partner program for system integrators, and its own marketplace where companies like Salesforce, IBM, and Zendesk offer ready-made voice agents. items.full: Anthropic has released Claude for Manufacturing, a plugin giving the AI direct access to industrial software to automate factory workflows. The new solution connects via four universal interfaces to Autodesk Fusion, Oracle NetSuite, Microsoft 365, and Infor. Other systems can be integrated through file exports to Microsoft 365. With 17 specific skills , the AI drafts quotes from actual inventory, compares suppliers, generates quality reports and design variants, and analyzes sensor data and manuals during machine downtime. Via an added Infor plugin, Claude can also order from backup suppliers when deliveries are delayed and reschedule production—after human approval. All results are linked to original source documents for employee review before reaching customers or suppliers. The plugin is available to Team and Enterprise customers but doesn't control physical machines yet. For that, Anthropic is separately developing the Model Hardware Standard as a research preview, connecting AI agents to devices like robotic arms and microscopes via standardized drivers. This cuts setup time from weeks or months to hours or minutes but still requires human oversight due to the AI's limited grasp of physical processes. items.full: AI company Runway has released its robot model Praxis-1 with open weights and source code. The model uses what it learned from video to control robots and shows promising results in the company's own tests. Runway has released Praxis-1, its AI model for controlling robots. The company first introduced Praxis-1 in late September but initially gave access only to select partners. Alongside the release, Runway published a detailed research report with new performance tests. Runway's model weights and source code are available under the Apache 2.0 license, which allows commercial use. Ad Praxis-1 takes in camera images, text instructions, and information about a robot's position. From those inputs, it predicts how the environment will change and calculates the right robot movements. As new camera frames come in, the model continuously adjusts its control. Ad Praxis-1 builds on a video model that learned how objects move and interact from ordinary footage. Runway then fine-tuned it with videos of human actions and robot data. This approach could reduce the need for expensive robot-specific datasets, which have traditionally been collected just to train these kinds of systems. Runway is best known for generative video models like Gen-4.5 . With Praxis-1, the company is bringing its video research into robotics. Runway calls Praxis-1 a World Action Model that predicts how a scene will change and derives matching robot movements from those predictions. Since September, robotics companies Standard Bots, Noble Machines, and Ultra have been testing Praxis-1 on different systems, including a humanoid robot, an industrial robot arm, and a dual-arm warehouse robot. Ad Praxis-1 still needs some specialized robot data. To adapt it to a Franka robot arm, Runway used about 277 hours of recordings from the public DROID research dataset, according to its research report . Those recordings show robots grasping and moving objects, for example. For a dual-arm robot, the company used between 1,400 and 2,600 hours of training material. Runway had already used DROID data and data from other robot systems during earlier training stages. Whether the approach actually needs less robot data overall than comparable models without general video pretraining is still an open question. On Nvidia's RoboLab-120 leaderboard , Praxis-1 scores a 46.2 percent success rate. The benchmark tests how reliably robot models can sort, grasp, or stack objects across 120 tasks in simulation. FLUX 3 Action , also built as a World Action Model, scores 42.9 percent under the same test conditions. That puts Praxis-1 at the top of the World Action Model category. In the overall leaderboard, it ranks fifth behind two AI agents and two robot models with different architectures. Runway ran all the tests itself, and the results haven't been independently verified yet. Ad After fine-tuning on DROID data, Runway tested the model on a real Franka robot arm. Both models had to complete the same ten tasks, like placing a banana on a plate or closing a drawer. With ten attempts per task, Praxis-1 succeeded 88 times, while FLUX 3 Action managed 80. items.title: OpenAI reassigns robotics researchers to other teams as general-purpose models might make specialized robotics AI unnecessary
items.desc: OpenAI is dissolving its standalone robotics team for the second time, but not because it lacks data. General-purpose models like GPT-6 Astra can apparently control robots directly, making a dedicated unit unnecessary. The researchers are being redistributed across other teams in what the company frames as a way to accelerate its robotics efforts. The article OpenAI reassigns robotics researchers to other teams as general-purpose models might make specialized robotics AI unnecessary appeared first on The Decoder .
items.full: OpenAI is apparently disbanding its robotics team again, but this time for different reasons than in 2020. Rather than abandoning robotics, the company wants to accelerate it by folding researchers into other teams. Robotics researchers are moving to the main research team under Chief Research Officer Mark Chen, while the applied robotics and hardware teams join Greg Brockman's Applied organization. OpenAI made the decision on such short notice that it had already booked a booth at the Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) in Austin, which then sat empty, Fortune reports . OpenAI apparently believes that general-purpose models like GPT-6 Astra can control robots directly , reducing the need for specialized robotics models. Ad In an Nvidia study , an Astra-powered agent achieved a 74.8 percent success rate on simulated robotics tasks, compared to 51 percent for the best specialized models. The tests used a simulated DROID robot, not a physical one. Ad A new robotics benchmark called StationeryBench compared GPT-6 Astra with Ai2's MolmoAct2 on five tasks involving desk objects on dual-arm YAM robotic arms. Across 200 trials, Astra fully completed 7 out of 100 tasks, while MolmoAct2 didn't complete a single one. Astra's average progress score was 46, compared to 12 for MolmoAct2. In another test, Astra running on a humanoid robot navigated and cleaned up a kitchen. It remains unclear how much robotics data OpenAI and others incorporated during training. Other large general-purpose models from Anthropic and Google have also made recent progress on robotics tasks. Specialized robotics models may still have advantages in cost and reliability as well as speed and energy consumption , even if they don't generalize as well. Ad Yoav Artzi , an AI researcher at Cornell University and Google DeepMind, also sees Astra as a major leap in spatial understanding . On the still-unpublished REMAP benchmark, GPT-6 Astra reaches near-human accuracy, according to Artzi. He suspects that OpenAI may have trained the model on large amounts of 3D training data such as Blender scenes. OpenAI shut down its robotics division in 2020 because, according to co-founder Wojciech Zaremba, the company lacked the training data it needed and large language models were a faster path to AGI. The company rebuilt the team in 2024. CEO Sam Altman is reportedly targeting a first public robot demo for 2027 , and OpenAI wants to build its own everyday robots in the long term. But the company also faces heavy financial pressure to focus on its core AI business , where it has lost significant ground to Anthropic .
